title: Optimize Model Usage in Ralph Loop
description: Implement economic optimization strategies for model selection in the agentic coding loop. The central problem: reasoning is expensive (Opus/Sonnet) but typing is cheap (Haiku). This epic covers 5 key optimization techniques to balance token budget against effectiveness.
design:
## Overview
The Ralph Loop currently uses a single model for all tasks, which is economically inefficient. We need to implement intelligent model selection strategies.

## Core Techniques
1. **Escalation Protocol**: Waterfall strategy - try cheapest model first, escalate on failure
2. **Architect vs Intern Split**: Smart model writes tests, cheap model writes implementation
3. **Prompt Caching**: 90% discount on context reuse via Anthropic's prompt caching
4. **Context Pruning**: Surgical context feeding, only necessary files
5. **Diff-Only Feedback**: Flat token count across retries, avoid context rot

## Success Criteria
- Measurable reduction in token costs
- Maintained or improved success rates
- Clear model selection logic in supervisor.py

title: Implement Escalation Protocol (Try-Catch Pattern)
description: Implement waterfall model strategy: attempt tasks with cheapest model first, escalate to smarter models only on backpressure failure.
design:
## Algorithm
1. **Attempt 1 (Haiku)**: Try to fix with cheapest model
   - Cost: Tiny
   - Success Rate: High for syntax, typos, simple logic
   - Backpressure Check: If verify_cmd passes → Commit & Exit
   - Failure: Revert with git reset --hard

2. **Attempt 2 (Sonnet)**: Escalate on Haiku failure
   - Cost: Moderate
   - Success Rate: High for refactoring, standard features
   - Prompt: 'Haiku failed to fix this. Here is the task. Think step-by-step.'

3. **(Optional) Attempt 3 (Opus)**: Final escalation for complex tasks

## Implementation
- Modify supervisor.py to accept model list instead of single model
- Pass list like: ['claude-3-haiku', 'claude-3-haiku', 'claude-3-5-sonnet']
- Loop through models, verify after each attempt
- Reset git state between attempts

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] supervisor.py accepts --models flag with comma-separated list
- [ ] Loop tries each model in sequence
- [ ] Git reset happens between attempts
- [ ] Success exits early (doesn't try all models)
- [ ] Logs show which model succeeded
acceptance_criteria: supervisor.py accepts --models flag, loops through models with git reset between attempts, exits early on success

title: Implement Architect vs Intern Split (Test-Driven Model Selection)
description: Use expensive model (Opus/Sonnet) to write tests, cheap model (Haiku) to write implementation. This is the highest-leverage optimization technique.
design:
## Strategy
**Smart Model (Opus/Sonnet)** writes the Bead specification and verification test:
- Cost: High, but one-time
- Task: 'Write a Pytest case that fails if the MarketData class doesn't handle 404 errors correctly'
- Why: Writing correct tests requires high reasoning. Wrong tests make the whole loop worthless.

**Cheap Model (Haiku)** writes the implementation:
- Cost: Low
- Task: 'Run this test. It failed. Write code to make it pass.'
- Why: Haiku excels at Red-Green-Refactor loops. The goal is rigid (pass the test), no architecture thinking needed.

## Implementation Approach
1. **Bead Generation Phase** (Sonnet/Opus):
   - Analyze project structure
   - Generate beads.json with task specifications
   - Generate test_*.py files with clear assertions

2. **Implementation Phase** (Haiku):
   - Read the test file
   - Read the error message
   - Write minimal code to pass the test
   - Iterate until green

## Workflow Integration
- Modify supervisor.py to support two-phase execution
- Phase 1: Use smart model for test generation (--test-model)
- Phase 2: Use cheap model for implementation (--impl-model)
- Store test files in version control as backpressure artifacts

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test generation uses Sonnet/Opus
- [ ] Implementation uses Haiku
- [ ] Tests are written before implementation starts
- [ ] Haiku receives test output and error messages
- [ ] Token costs show measurable reduction
acceptance_criteria: Two-phase execution with smart model for tests and Haiku for implementation, measurable token cost reduction

title: Implement Prompt Caching (90% Discount Strategy)
description: Leverage Anthropic's Prompt Caching to cache static context (repo structure, docs) and pay only for dynamic content (errors, tasks). Enables 90% cost reduction and significant speed improvements on retry iterations.
design:
## The Problem
Without caching: Every loop iteration re-reads the entire codebase
- Retry 1: Pay to read 50 files
- Retry 2: Pay to read 50 files again
- Retry 3: Pay to read 50 files again

With caching: Pay once, subsequent reads are 90% cheaper and faster
- Retry 1: Pay full price (cache miss)
- Retry 2-N: Pay 10% (cache hit)

## Implementation Strategy
Structure prompts with static context at top, dynamic at bottom:



## Technical Details
- Use Anthropic's cache_control parameter
- Mark static blocks with cache breakpoints
- Keep dynamic instructions at the end
- Cache invalidates on static content change
- Monitor cache hit rates via API metrics

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Prompts structured with static/dynamic sections
- [ ] cache_control parameters set correctly in API calls
- [ ] Repo dumps and docs marked as cacheable
- [ ] Dynamic task/error info not cached
- [ ] Metrics show cache hit rates >70%
- [ ] Token costs reduced by ~60-80% on retries
acceptance_criteria: Prompts use cache_control, static context cached, cache hit rate >70%, token costs reduced 60-80% on retries

title: Implement Context Pruning (Malloc Discipline)
description: Implement surgical context feeding - only provide the agent with files it needs for the specific task. Avoid feeding entire repository, which wastes tokens and degrades performance.
design:
## The Anti-Pattern
Bad: 'Here is my project. Fix the bug in utils.py.' (Reads 50 files)
- Wastes tokens on irrelevant context
- Increases latency
- Can confuse the model

## The Solution
Good: 'Here is utils.py and test_utils.py. Fix the bug.' (Reads 2 files)
- Surgical precision
- Minimal token usage
- Clear focus

## Implementation Approaches

### Option 1: Explicit Context in Beads
Add context_files field to bead specification:
{
  "id": "005",
  "instruction": "Implement get_price()",
  "context_files": ["src/market.py", "tests/test_market.py"]
}

Supervisor only cat's these specific files into prompt.

### Option 2: Repository Map
- Use tool like repomap (from Aider) or ctags
- Provide agent with map/index of repo
- Agent requests specific files it needs
- Supervisor fetches and injects

### Option 3: Smart Context Selection
- Analyze task description
- Use grep/semantic search to find relevant files
- Auto-select test files matching implementation files
- Include dependency imports

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Beads support context_files specification
- [ ] Supervisor only loads specified files
- [ ] Default to current file + test file if not specified
- [ ] Option to generate repo map for agent reference
- [ ] Metrics show reduced tokens per task
- [ ] Context size <10 files for 90% of tasks
acceptance_criteria: Beads specify context_files, supervisor loads only those files, context size <10 files for most tasks

title: Implement context builder to load specified files
Implement Diff-Only Feedback Loop (Prevent Context Rot)
description: On retry attempts, send only essential information instead of entire conversation history. Prevents linear token growth (N, 2N, 3N...) across iterations.
design:
## The Problem: Context Rot
Traditional approach includes full conversation history:
- Retry 1: 1000 tokens
- Retry 2: 2000 tokens (includes all of retry 1)
- Retry 3: 3000 tokens (includes retry 1 + 2)
- Result: Linear growth, expensive failures

## The Solution: Diff-Only Feedback
Send only essential information on each retry:
1. **The Goal** (Static) - The original task description
2. **Attempted Code** (The diff that failed) - git diff output
3. **Error Message** (The stderr) - What went wrong

Omit the chat history, previous attempts, and meta-discussion.

Result: Flat token count across all retries (~1000 tokens each)

## Implementation Details

### Retry Prompt Structure
Previous context: [OMITTED]
Task: Implement get_price() function
Previous attempt failed.

Code attempted:
--- a/src/market.py
+++ b/src/market.py
@@ -10,0 +11,3 @@
+def get_price():
+    return data.price

Error output:
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'price'

Please fix the error and implement correctly.

### Technical Approach
- Use git diff to capture attempted changes
- Extract stderr from test output
- Create fresh prompt for each retry (don't append)
- Maintain goal statement as constant
- Track retry count for escalation logic

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Retry prompts don't include conversation history
- [ ] Each retry includes: goal + diff + error
- [ ] Token count flat across retries (variance <10%)
- [ ] git diff used to show attempted code
- [ ] Test stderr cleanly extracted and included
- [ ] Metrics show 3x-5x token reduction on multi-retry tasks
acceptance_criteria: Retry prompts exclude history, include only goal/diff/error, token count flat across retries

title: Factory Configuration - YAML-based Project Adapter
description:
Add YAML-based configuration support to supervisor.py to enable per-project customization of agent and verify commands. This makes the orchestrator adaptable across different projects (Python/Go/etc.) without hardcoding defaults.

Configuration Priority: CLI Args > agent.yaml > Hardcoded Defaults

Key capabilities:
- Read agent.yaml from target project directory
- Support verify_cmd and agent_cmd overrides
- Graceful fallback to defaults
- Maintain backward compatibility

title: Add validation and error handling for config
description:
Enhance configuration loading with proper validation and error handling:

- Validate YAML structure (ensure it's a dict)
- Handle FileNotFoundError gracefully
- Handle yaml.YAMLError with helpful messages
- Verify {prompt} placeholder exists in agent_cmd
- Log configuration source for debugging

This ensures the tool never breaks due to malformed config files.

title: Add PyYAML dependency and config loading function
description:
Add PyYAML to requirements.txt and implement load_config() function that reads agent.yaml from current working directory.

Implementation:

- Create load_config() function that:
  - Checks for agent.yaml in os.getcwd()
  - Returns parsed YAML as dict
  - Returns empty dict if file not found
  - Handles YAML parsing errors gracefully with warning message
  
Files:
- requirements.txt: Add PyYAML
- supervisor.py: Add load_config() function before RalphLoop class

title: Refactor argument resolution with config priority system
description:
